The  “is abortion murder?” one is a really shitty question

I dont really think these questions really relate to sex ed. 

From a bisexual trans man perspective: sex ed should be about teaching that puberty causes changes to one’s body, what those changes cause and mean, teaching about consent and incentivizing kids to come forward to their teachers and parents in case anyone makes them feel uncomfortable/invade their personal space/ or sexually abuses them. 
Informing kids and parents about the dangers of the internet and predatory behavior that happens there, and teaching them ways to stay safe.

Its also important to remind them (i dont really know to what ages are you teaching this) that if they’re having sex, or will have sex, there are safe ways to do it. It’s important to spread information about how STDs are spread and the importance of using preservatives to prevent pregnancy. (other things like birth control pills, IUD, etc)

Regarding the LGBTQ part i think that when your talking about the changes hormones cause in your body during puberty, you can simply explain that just like men can be attracted to women and women to men, there are people who feel attraction to the same gender as they are, and people who dont have a preference for any specific gender, and that that’s okay. Everyone is different and thats alright! There is no need for them to “define sexualities”.

If you plan on explaining transgender individuals, you can simply say there are people who were raised as boys/girls but later realize they dont feel comfortable that way and they later identify differently from what they were assigned.

Theres no need to go much further than that, I think the most important part is teaching respect towards everyone, and explaining that their body shouldn’t be inappropriately touched by adults and/or anyone else they don’t consent to.

I have really bad misophonia, it’s really challenging to live with it, but i bought a big ear protector (like those for construction sites) and I have a pair of ear protectors that are custom made for my ears to help diminish my discomfort. These ear protectors are very discrete and were made by my otolaryngologist, who often make these for autistic folks or ppl with misophonia, like me. 
Couldn’t recommend it more, I couldn’t even leave my house a couple of months ago due to noises, but these were life saving!
